description: Laser SDK: agent memory, durable workflows, sessions and messaging on Apache Iggy, with matching Rust, Python and TypeScript clients.
rules: Never print or log the connection string or its password. Read it from LASER_CONNECTION_STRING inside the program.
Connect with Laser.connect_env() in Python, Laser.connectEnv() in TypeScript or Laser::connect_env() in Rust. Each reads the connection string from LASER_CONNECTION_STRING.
A LaserData API key is not a connection string. Copy the connection string from the deployment's Credentials tab in the Console.
Python installs with python -m pip install laser-sdk and imports laser_sdk. TypeScript installs @laserdata/laser-sdk and runs with npx tsx.
Rust adds laser-sdk with the agent and kv features, tokio with macros, rt-multi-thread and time, serde with derive, serde_json, and async-trait for a step that awaits.
Start from the two complete programs at the top of each README. The examples folder holds them as workflow and memory-correction (workflow.py and memory_correction.py in Python).

The workflow program runs three in-process steps, one awaiting a one second sleep, and prints its outcome as JSON: step(label, run=...) in Python, stepLocal(label, run) in TypeScript, step_local(label, run) in Rust.
A step's run is a plain or async function (a type implementing StepFn in Rust), gets the earlier outputs by label as bytes, and returns str or bytes. outcome.text(label) decodes one output.
WorkflowOutcome carries run_id, status (completed), completed_steps in completion order, outputs by label as bytes, and text(label). A failed step raises StepFailedError.
In Python memory(namespace), workflow(name), step(...) and sessions() return at once. Await connect_env(), memory_topic(...), remember, supersede, recall, forget and workflow.run().
The memory program corrects a fact for one user with memory.supersede(old_id, new_fact), then recalls and prints the current facts.
Work in a scratch stream that is deleted at the end: async with laser.scratch_stream(prefix) as scratch in Python, await using scratch = await laser.scratchStream(prefix) in TypeScript.
In Rust call laser.scratch_stream(prefix), then scratch.delete(). To keep what the program writes, name a stream: LASER_STREAM, with_default_stream(name), or connect_env(stream=name).

The stream option of connect_env is Laser.connect_env(stream=name) in Python, Laser.connectEnvWithStream(name) in TypeScript and Laser::connect_env_with_stream(name) in Rust. It wins over LASER_STREAM.
A workflow run and the first memory write create their stream and topics, so they need no bootstrap call.
Correct a remembered fact with supersede, which forgets the old fact in every conversation. A default recall reads the writes the same connection made.

recall returns MemoryItem objects newest first (item.text() in Python and Rust, memoryItemText(item) in TypeScript). A semantic query ranks every fact by the words it shares with the query and drops none.
Use the SDK's own workflow, memory and session APIs for durable results. A local list, dict or plain function is not durable.
A LaserData Cloud deployment admits a Laser SDK connection only from an address its access rules allow over TCP.
